question: True or false: sending a probe from Earth into the Sun takes more change of speed than sending it out of the solar system?
answer: True. Earth carries everything round the Sun at about 30 km/s; to fall in, a probe must cancel nearly all of that, while leaving the solar system takes only about 12 km/s more. Parker Solar Probe, which merely grazes the Sun, left in a window timed for Venus, whose seven flybys shed its speed.
move: Moving sideways fast makes the centre the hardest place to reach.
trap: Picturing the Sun as downhill, so falling in must be easy.

diagram.caption: Falling in means cancelling nearly all of Earth's 30 km/s; escaping takes 12 more.

source: Fox et al., Space Science Reviews, 2016
